transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?
Since my husband passed, it feels like everything inside me just shut down, and I can’t make myself do the things I used to care about. I just don't have it in me anymore to keep up with my life.
How long have you been feeling this way since your husband passed away?
It started creeping in during the first year after he passed away. This numb, shut-down feeling has been pretty much the same for a little over two years now.
Have your symptoms been present most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks at a time during this period?

Yes, it's like this almost every single day, most of the day. This heavy, shut-down feeling has been constant for over two years now, and hearing his voice and getting stuck has been happening regularly for the past few months. It's been going on much longer than just two weeks; it just doesn't seem to stop.
Have you completely lost interest in activities you used to enjoy, or do you still feel some pleasure when doing certain things, even if it's less than before?

It really feels like someone turned a switch off inside me, and I’ve completely lost interest in everything. Things I used to love, like my choir, quilting, and cooking Sunday dinners, just feel heavy and so far away now. I don't get any pleasure from them at all anymore.
Have you experienced any feelings of worthlessness, guilt, or thoughts that life isn’t worth living since your husband passed away?
No, I wouldn't say I feel guilty or have thoughts of ending my life. It's more that I just feel completely empty, numb, and shut down inside.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a prolonged and persistent emotional response to the death of her husband, characterized by pervasive numbness, loss of interest, and functional decline lasting over two years. The symptoms are consistent with adjustment disorder with prolonged depressive reaction, as they began within a year of the stressor and have persisted for more than six months beyond the expected period of acute grief.
